verdict.rationale: Pylon documents official mobile SDKs for iOS, Android and React Native, plus a JavaScript API for its chat widget, so official SDKs exist. Their scope is limited to embedding and customizing the chat widget. Its general platform API is documented only as a REST/OpenAPI surface, with no official client SDK in evidence. The published OpenAPI spec is a building block for generating clients, not an SDK itself. Missing for 10: official server-side/language client SDKs (e.g., Python/TypeScript) for the core Pylon API, SDK reference docs beyond chat-widget embedding, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Embed Pylon's chat widget in your iOS, Android, or React Native application.
Pylon's mobile SDKs allow you to embed the chat widget directly in your mobile app, providing users with in-app support without leaving your application.
